brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
An all-bud green tea from Pingli county in Ankang, Shaanxi, named for the Nüwa heritage sites of the area. The local soils are noted for selenium and zinc.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It took a gold award at a western China tea fair in 2002 and a first prize at the fifth Zhongcha Cup in 2003. It was also recommended by the China Tea Marketing Association at a Shaanxi tea show in 2003. Little is documented about its origins before these awards.
processing: Fixed, rolled and dried; about ten jin of fresh leaf gives only a few liang of finished tea.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Whole buds, slightly flattened and even.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
